definitions.explanation: The column of vertebrae running down the center of the back, supporting the body's structure.
Figuratively, the central support or foundation of something — an organization, system, or argument.

examples.japanese: {背骨|せぼね}が{曲|ま}がっている。
{転|ころ}んで{背骨|せぼね}を{痛|いた}めた。
examples.english: I fell and hurt my spine.

examples.japanese: {姿勢|しせい}が{悪|わる}いと{背骨|せぼね}に{負担|ふたん}がかかる。
examples.english: Poor posture puts strain on the spine.

examples.japanese: {製造業|せいぞうぎょう}はこの{国|くに}の{経済|けいざい}の{背骨|せぼね}だ。
examples.english: Manufacturing is the backbone of this country's economy.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{組織|そしき}の{背骨|せぼね}となる{存在|そんざい}だ。
examples.english: He is the backbone of the organization.

examples.japanese: {背骨|せぼね}のない{計画|けいかく}は{失敗|しっぱい}する。
examples.english: A plan without a backbone will fail.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {背|せ} (back) and {骨|ほね} (bone). In its literal sense, it is the everyday word for spine. The figurative sense of 'core support' mirrors English 'backbone.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {背骨|せぼね}が{曲|ま}がる (the spine curves)
- {背骨|せぼね}を{伸|の}ばす (to straighten the spine)
- {背骨|せぼね}を{矯正|きょうせい}する (to correct the spine)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {脊椎|せきつい}: vertebral column — the medical/anatomical term for the spine
